question: An architect is setting conventions for what agents should write into scratchpad files during a large codebase exploration. Which content best serves the goal of counteracting context degradation on later questions?
options: A) A single vague note such as 'explored the codebase and things generally look fine,' without further detail.
B) Concrete facts such as exact class names, file paths, and discovered mechanisms, recorded as they are found.
C) Only a timestamp of when each exploration step occurred, without any description of what was found.
D) The complete raw contents of every file the agent opened during the investigation, copied in full into the scratchpad.
correct_answers: B) Concrete facts such as exact class names, file paths, and discovered mechanisms, recorded as they are found.
explanations: Incorrect. A vague summary provides nothing specific to anchor later answers and does not prevent the agent from falling back on generic assumptions.
Correct. Specific, concrete findings are exactly what later questions need to avoid drifting into generic 'typical pattern' language, giving the agent something precise to reference.
Incorrect. Timestamps without any description of findings give the coordinator no usable information about what was actually discovered.
Incorrect. Copying full raw file contents defeats the purpose of a scratchpad, reintroducing the same volume of data the agent was trying to avoid keeping in active context.
